knowledge:
- key_parameters: genomicVariants=Path to a VCF/MAF file or a VRanges object containing genomic variants ;; aggregateRecords=Logical; set to TRUE when input contains multiple samples to aggregate records ;; minSizeKataegis=Minimum number of variants in a segment to be classified as kataegis (default is 6) ;; IMDcutoff=Intermutation distance cutoff (default is 1000) or a custom function defining the cutoff per segment ;; refSeq=A data frame containing sequence lengths, used when analyzing non-standard reference sequences ;; showSegmentation=Logical; in rainfallPlot(), visualizes detected segments with their mean IMD ;; showKataegis=Logical; in rainfallPlot(), highlights putative kataegis foci ;; showSequence=Character; in rainfallPlot(), displays specific chromosomes or "Kataegis" to show chromosomes with detected foci
- alternatives: maftools, ClusteredMutations, SeqKat, kataegis, and SigProfilerClusters are mentioned as alternative packages for kataegis detection, but katdetectr is preferred for its integration into the Bioconductor ecosystem and its changepoint-based segmentation approach
- when_to_use: Use this package when analyzing somatic genomic variants (SNVs, InDels) from cancer genomes to identify and visualize localized hypermutation clusters (kataegis)
- pitfalls: Overlapping genomic variants (e.g., an InDel and SNV) must be reduced, which detectKataegis() handles automatically. For multi-sample files (like MAF), failing to set aggregateRecords = TRUE may lead to incorrect IMD calculations if records are not aggregated. Analyzing non-standard reference sequences (other than hg19/hg38) requires providing a custom sequence length data frame via the refSeq argument to avoid errors.

workflows.name: standard_kataegis_detection
workflows.intent: Detect and visualize kataegis foci from standard genomic variant files (VCF or MAF) or VRanges objects.
input: pathToMAF (MAF file containing genomic variants from single or multiple samples)
workflows.stages: 1. Import genomic variants from VCF, MAF, or generate synthetic data using generateSyntheticData() ;; 2. Detect kataegis foci using detectKataegis() ;; 3. Summarize and inspect the KatDetect object using summary(), print(), or show() ;; 4. Extract underlying data (variants, segments, foci, info) using getter functions getGenomicVariants(), getSegments(), getKataegisFoci(), and getInfo() ;; 5. Visualize results using rainfallPlot()
workflows.code:
pathToVCF <- system.file(package = "katdetectr", "extdata/CPTAC_Breast.vcf")
pathToMAF <- system.file(package = "katdetectr", "extdata/APL_primary.maf")
syntheticData <- generateSyntheticData(nBackgroundVariants = 2500, nKataegisFoci = 1)
kdVCF <- detectKataegis(genomicVariants = pathToVCF)
kdMAF <- detectKataegis(genomicVariants = pathToMAF, aggregateRecords = TRUE)
kdSynthetic <- detectKataegis(genomicVariants = syntheticData)
summary(kdVCF)
print(kdVCF)
show(kdVCF)
kdVCF
getGenomicVariants(kdVCF)
getSegments(kdVCF)
getKataegisFoci(kdVCF)
getInfo(kdVCF)
rainfallPlot(kdVCF)
rainfallPlot(kdMAF, showSegmentation = TRUE)
rainfallPlot(kdSynthetic, showKataegis = TRUE, showSegmentation = TRUE, showSequence = "Kataegis")

workflows.name: custom_cutoff_kataegis_detection
workflows.intent: Detect kataegis foci using a custom user-defined function to calculate segment-specific IMD cutoffs.
workflows.stages: 1. Define custom functions for modeling sample rate and calculating segment-specific IMD cutoffs ;; 2. Run detectKataegis() with the custom function passed to the IMDcutoff parameter

workflows.name: non_standard_sequence_detection
workflows.intent: Detect kataegis foci in genomes with non-standard sequences by providing custom sequence lengths.
input: syndata (VRanges object containing variants on non-standard sequences)
sequenceLength (data frame containing the lengths of the non-standard sequences)
workflows.stages: 1. Prepare genomic variants with non-standard sequence names ;; 2. Construct a data frame containing the lengths of the non-standard sequences ;; 3. Run detectKataegis() specifying the refSeq argument
workflows.code:
syndata1 <- generateSyntheticData(seqnames = c("chr1_gl000191_random", "chr4_ctg9_hap1"))
syndata2 <- generateSyntheticData(seqnames = "chr1")
syndata <- suppressWarnings(c(syndata1, syndata2))

sequenceLength <- data.frame(
    chr1 = 249250621,
    chr1_gl000191_random = 106433,
    chr4_ctg9_hap1 = 590426
)

kdNonStandard <- detectKataegis(genomicVariants = syndata, refSeq = sequenceLength)
